thread.title: Stock News Today: Apple Hit Again As Dow Jones Slumps Nearly 600 Points | Investor's Business Daily

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Stock News Today: Apple Hit Again As Dow Jones Slumps Nearly 600 Points | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market has had plenty of headlines to worry about in recent weeks, including the trade war with China, weakness in FANG stocks and the path of interest rate hikes by the Fed, just to name a few. In stock news today, retail earnings reports from Target ( TGT ), Kohl's ( KSS ), Ross Stores ( ROST ), TJX Companies ( TJX ) and Lowe's ( LOW ) were in focus, and the news wasn't good as many warned of potentially soft holiday sales.
The Nasdaq composite slumped 2.8% early, undercutting its Oct. 29 intraday low and effectively killing its rally attempt that started on Oct. 30. But it was well off session lows in late-afternoon trading, down just 1.7%. The Dow Jones industrial average was down 2% and the S&P 500 lost 1.8%.
The Dow Jones and S&P 500 are still holding above their Oct. 29 lows, so their rallies are technically intact. Volume on the NYSE and Nasdaq was tracking about 20% higher than Monday's levels in the stock market today.
Stock News Today: Apple Hit Again Apple ( AAPL ) lagged in the Dow Jones again, down 4%, after Goldman Sachs lowered its price target to 182 from 209.
Retail chain stores Ross Stores, O'Reilly Automotive ( ORLY ), Costco ( COST ) and Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) underperformed in the Nasdaq 100 with losses of 3% to 8%.
Bright spots in the Nasdaq 100 included semiconductor stocks Applied Materials ( AMAT ), Analog Devices ( ADI ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ). After slumping nearly 4% Monday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor index was down 0.4% in late trading.
In other stock news today, Boeing ( BA ) shares lost 1% after the company canceled a call regarding last month's Lion Air 737 Max crash . A Wall Street Journal report said that Boeing failed to disclose possible issues with the flight control system on its new jets before the Lion Air incident.
Oil and gas-related industry groups were among the day's worst performers as oil prices fell sharply. At the New York Mercantile Exchange, U.S. crude oil futures slumped 7%, to $53.21 a barrel. Brent crude, the European benchmark also fell 7%, to $62.28 a barrel.
Weekly inventory data Wednesday could show a ninth straight increase in supplies.
Inside the IBD 50 , Innoviva ( INVA ) added 0.6%, to 16.58, as it works on a cup-with-handle base with a 16.94 buy point .
